solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: What to watch for the score!

definitions.text: What to watch for the score!

parts.words: What to watch for the score!
parts.note: a photographer tells sitters to watch this little bird, and in golf it is a score of one under par

explanation.surface: Someone at a match is told to keep an eye on the scoreboard.
explanation.walkthrough: Two senses meet: the photographer's old catchphrase 'watch the birdie', and the golf score one stroke under par.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers record a hole played in one stroke under par with this name, and photographers ask people to watch one.

definitions.meaning: a long loaf with diagonal slashes across its top crust, sold by bakers

explanation.surface: Mistakes made by staff in a bakery.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is both a blunder and a British style of crusty white loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A blunder is informally called a bloomer in Britain, and a bloomer is also a loaf made by bakers.

clue.text: Stop and go for each vegetable

parts.note: red is the traffic-light colour meaning stop
pep means energy or vigour, as in 'get up and go'
per means for each, as in 'per head'

explanation.surface: Traffic-light instructions somehow leading to a vegetable for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop and go' suggests traffic lights; only the stop gives a colour, while 'go' is energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A capsicum of the ripe crimson kind is a common salad and cooking vegetable.

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral, plus 's
ay is an old poetic word for always, also spelt aye

explanation.surface: A person who is constantly astonished by things.
explanation.definitionFit: This old-fashioned British exclamation is uttered when someone is startled or shocked.

clue.text: Worker at dance is a sport

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A worker at a dance claims that dancing is a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A team game played by throwing a ball into a goal, popular in continental Europe.

indicators.note: cut means the word for cells loses its final letter

parts.note: asci are the spore-bearing cells of certain fungi, plural of ascus
ended means stopped or finished

explanation.surface: A rose was pruned, its cells cut, and then it stopped growing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like the flower but is the past tense of rise. ASCI, plural of ascus, loses its last letter to give ASC.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs in the past tense mean climbed or went upward.

clue.text: Waving hand and turning neck. So, thanks!

indicators.note: waving shakes the letters of the word hand about
turning makes the letters of neck and so spin into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone waves and turns their head while saying a grateful farewell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waving' and 'turning' both act as anagram signals: HAND, NECK and SO are shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: This German phrase is the standard way to express gratitude, much like 'thank you very much'.

indicators.note: in a down clue, topped means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a parson is a parish priest

explanation.surface: A clergyman is executed for a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topped' suggests killed, but here it means the word loses its top letter, P.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately setting fire to property is a criminal offence.

clue.text: I sail out east to get in touch

indicators.note: out signals the letters of I sail are rearranged

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A sailor heads east to make contact with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To act as a go-between or keep in contact with another party.

definitions.meaning: a card game such as canasta at 11 across begins with me handing out the cards
a model or perfect example to aim for

explanation.surface: How I open a game is the standard method.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as I DEAL: any card game, canasta included, starts with dealing.
explanation.definitionFit: A benchmark of perfection, as in a model to follow.

definitions.meaning: a card game in which players pair cards and avoid holding the odd queen
an older unmarried woman, a dated term

explanation.surface: An unmarried woman who is up for anything.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated term for an unmarried older woman, and also a children's card game.

indicators.note: abandoned means the abbreviation for railway is dropped from the bird

parts.note: a canary is a yellow songbird

explanation.surface: A bird has deserted a disused railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned railway station' reads as one disused place, but 'abandoned' acts on the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A rummy-type card game for partners, developed in Uruguay.

definitions.meaning: suitable or proper, an old adjective
a gathering of riders and hounds before a hunt sets off

explanation.surface: Is someone in good enough shape for the fox hunt?
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adjective for suitable, and the assembly point of a fox hunt.

indicators.note: mangled, as linen through an old wringer, means the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone at a royal court wants their linen put through the mangle.
explanation.walkthrough: A mangle is an old laundry wringer, so 'mangled' fits the linen. 'Court' suggests royalty but is the playing area.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket game played on a court, originally on grass.

clue.text: No runs scored by chief at Berkshire town

parts.note: in cricket, a maiden is an over in which no runs are scored
a head is a leader or chief

explanation.surface: A cricket chief fails to score at a ground in Berkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden over is a cricket over of six balls yielding no runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A Thames-side town in the English county of Berkshire.

clue.text: Agent, amateur, at match after draw

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative or agent
lay means non-professional, as in a lay person

explanation.surface: An agent and an amateur attend a match after a lottery draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' suggests a lottery or raffle; it is a tied game.
explanation.definitionFit: In knockout competitions a tied game is often played again, a second fixture.

definitions.meaning: timber panels or posts that enclose a field or garden
swordplay with foil, épée or sabre

explanation.surface: Wooden barriers protect a sports ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guarding' is a link here, though it also hints at a fencer's guard.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a set of timber barriers and the Olympic sport of swordplay.

indicators.note: affected means altered, so the letters of countries are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Nations hit by some event made people anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: People prone to excessive anxiety or obsessive worry.

clue.text: State having Tyneside support about request

parts.note: Tyneside is in north-east England, abbreviated NE

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the support goes round the request

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
to ask is to request

explanation.surface: A state whose people back a Tyneside appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside is the Newcastle area in north-east England. 'about' means surrounding here, not turning back.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the fifty United States, in the Great Plains.

clue.text: I left Tony cavorting with girls vigorously

indicators.note: cavorting means prancing about, so the letters are mixed up
left means the letter I has departed from the word girls

explanation.surface: I walked out while Tony was frolicking with the girls in a lively way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I left' takes I out of GIRLS, leaving GRLS; 'cavorting' mixes those letters with TONY.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean in a forceful, energetic manner.

definitions.meaning: Robert ..., British Poet Laureate from 1913 to 1930
a verb: spans or links, as a structure over a river does
plural of the trick-taking card game for four players in pairs

explanation.surface: A poet backs card games.
explanation.definitionFit: Spans over rivers, the four-player card game, and the Poet Laureate Robert Bridges.

indicators.note: not signals that the word for is removed from the cheese

parts.note: Roquefort is a French blue cheese made from ewe's milk

explanation.surface: A claim that cheese does not help someone who has had a stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stroke' suggests illness; it is a shot in croquet.
explanation.definitionFit: In croquet, a shot in which a player's ball strikes another ball.

definitions.meaning: the runs that cricket batsmen put on the board
a score is a group of twenty, so 20s are multiples of twenty

explanation.surface: Batsmen tend to make twenties.
explanation.definitionFit: Totals of runs made in cricket, and an old word for groups of twenty.

definitions.meaning: Darby, of Darby and Joan, the devoted elderly couple; said the same way in Britain
the Epsom horse race for three-year-olds, a famous English flat race

explanation.surface: Joan's husband is off at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: Joan's partner is properly spelt DARBY; the clue relies on the British pronunciation of the race, so it is a setter's slip with no sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Epsom classic horse race, and the British-sounding partner in the proverbial old couple.

clue.text: Five shillings and singular dollar bills for 29?

parts.note: a crown was an old British coin worth five shillings
greens is slang for dollar bills; singular makes it one green

explanation.surface: Swapping old British money for dollars to spend on a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 29 across is BOWLING; this is a bowling lawn with a raised centre, common in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A type of lawn with a domed centre used for a regional form of bowls.

clue.text: A certain copper entered at the right moment

indicators.note: entered means the copper symbol goes inside the word for a certain

parts.note: one means a certain, as in 'one day'
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A particular policeman came in just in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman; it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom from theatre: an actor entering on a prompt arrives exactly when needed.

clue.text: Fruit gets cored for car sport

indicators.note: cored means the middle of the fruit is taken out

parts.note: a pomelo is a large citrus fruit like a grapefruit

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit is cored for a motor sport.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works twice: a Volkswagen model and a sport on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: Volkswagen makes a small hatchback with this name, and it is also a horseback team game.

clue.text: Affected the way engineers exercised for starters

indicators.note: for starters signals the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: The way engineers did warm-up exercises looked pretentious.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessively dainty or quaint in a way that seems put on.

indicators.note: making noises signals that words sound like the instruments

parts.note: racketts are Renaissance and baroque double-reed woodwind instruments

explanation.surface: Baroque instruments of sport produce noises.
explanation.walkthrough: Racketts were squat double-reed woodwinds of the Renaissance and baroque.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast indoor court game played with a hard ball, ancestor of squash.

indicators.note: in signals that the bird goes inside the singer's name

parts.note: Bing Crosby was an American crooner and actor
an owl is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: A bird in Crosby, Merseyside, delivering something.
explanation.walkthrough: Crosby suggests the Merseyside town, but it is the singer Bing Crosby.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolling a ball at pins in ten-pin; the question mark flags the loose definition.

clue.text: Wade off into Scottish river for sport

indicators.note: into signals that the shuffled letters go inside the river

parts.note: the Spey is a salmon river in north-east Scotland

indicators.note: off means the letters of wade are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone wades off into a Scottish river for some sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wade off' reads as a paddler leaving; 'off' is the anagram signal, giving EDWA, and 'into' places that within the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Motorcycle racing round an oval dirt track.

definitions.meaning: the largest of the Channel Islands
a race leader's shirt in the Tour de France, such as the yellow one

explanation.surface: An island tops the list on a holiday tour.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tour de France awards coloured shirts to its race leaders.
explanation.definitionFit: A Channel Island, and a knitted top or cycling shirt like the coveted maillot jaune.
